26.01.01.context: A company wants employees to sign in through its identity provider.
26.01.01.concept: SAML SSO exchanges signed assertions; validate issuer, audience, recipient, time and replay protection using a trusted library and metadata.
26.01.01.exercise: Draw SP-initiated sign-in, then test a disposable IdP with valid and invalid audience assertions.
26.01.01.positive: A valid assertion establishes the intended identity only.
26.01.01.negative: Wrong issuer, expired or replayed assertion must be denied.
26.01.01.boundary: Synthetic policy check on already-validated claims only; no actual SAML assertion, SCIM, MFA, token or identity-provider verification.

26.01.02.concept: SCIM provisioning synchronizes identities and groups; disabling identity must also revoke applicable access, not merely hide it.
26.01.02.exercise: Design a synthetic create/update/deactivate event sequence and test repeated delivery and deactivation.
26.01.02.positive: Disabled user loses intended access; repeated provisioning is safe.
26.01.02.boundary: Synthetic policy check on already-validated claims only; no actual SAML assertion, SCIM, MFA, token or identity-provider verification.

26.01.03.context: An admin claims a company's email domain.
26.01.03.concept: Domain ownership proof and organization membership are distinct; verify a scoped expiring challenge using the intended method.
26.01.03.exercise: Design a synthetic DNS challenge with random token, expiration and tenant binding; test mismatched token.
26.01.03.positive: Only the intended claimant completes verification.
26.01.03.negative: Email suffix alone cannot grant admin rights.
26.01.03.boundary: Synthetic policy check on already-validated claims only; no actual SAML assertion, SCIM, MFA, token or identity-provider verification.

26.01.04.context: An organization loses an employee laptop.
26.01.04.concept: Sessions and devices need revocation, expiry, refresh controls and server-side enforcement.
26.01.04.exercise: Use synthetic sessions for two devices; revoke one and exercise subsequent protected requests.
26.01.04.positive: Revoked session denied; unaffected session follows policy.
26.01.04.negative: UI-only revocation that leaves tokens active fails.
26.01.04.boundary: Synthetic policy check on already-validated claims only; no actual SAML assertion, SCIM, MFA, token or identity-provider verification.

26.01.05.context: A user initiates a high-risk settings change.
26.01.05.concept: Step-up authentication requires recent stronger evidence for sensitive actions; ordinary sign-in may be insufficient.
26.01.05.exercise: Evaluate enterpriseAccess with required MFA and missing claim; design an actual challenge and freshness test.
26.01.05.positive: Validated fresh second factor allows intended operation.
26.01.05.negative: Missing, stale or spoofed factor evidence fails.
26.01.05.boundary: Synthetic policy check on already-validated claims only; no actual SAML assertion, SCIM, MFA, token or identity-provider verification.

26.01.06.context: A tenant admin edits organization login requirements.
26.01.06.concept: Policy changes require authorization, scoped validation, safe rollout and recovery from lockout.
26.01.06.exercise: Design versioned policy updates with actor and change reason; test foreign-tenant change and recovery account policy.
26.01.06.negative: Cross-tenant update or irreversible lockout fails.
26.01.06.boundary: Synthetic policy check on already-validated claims only; no actual SAML assertion, SCIM, MFA, token or identity-provider verification.

26.01.07.context: An auditor investigates an administrative login.
26.01.07.concept: Audit records capture actor, action, target, outcome, time and correlation; secrets and raw assertions stay out.
26.01.07.exercise: Generate synthetic successful and rejected events; verify minimal fields and access restrictions.
26.01.07.positive: Both outcomes can be reconstructed without credentials.
26.01.07.negative: Missing denied event or sensitive token in audit fails.
26.01.07.boundary: Synthetic policy check on already-validated claims only; no actual SAML assertion, SCIM, MFA, token or identity-provider verification.

26.01.08.context: A learner reviews enterprise authentication threats.
26.01.08.concept: Model IdP trust, provisioning, sessions, MFA, tenant identity and admin control as separate boundaries.
26.01.08.exercise: Run enterpriseAccess tests; write an abuse-case matrix for assertion replay, deprovisioning and cross-tenant escalation.
26.01.08.positive: Each threat has denial test, owner and recovery plan.
26.01.08.negative: Trusting unvalidated claims or missing revocation evidence blocks acceptance.
26.01.08.boundary: Synthetic policy check on already-validated claims only; no actual SAML assertion, SCIM, MFA, token or identity-provider verification.

26.02.01.context: A subscription transitions through trial, active and unpaid states.
26.02.01.concept: Use explicit allowed transitions; provider status and application entitlement are related but distinct.
26.02.01.exercise: Create a synthetic state transition table and test active, canceled and expired dates in entitlement.
26.02.01.positive: Access matches the documented policy and cutoff.
26.02.01.negative: Unknown status or expired entitlement cannot grant access.
26.02.01.boundary: Synthetic entitlement policy; no payment provider authenticity, tax, invoicing, real charges or durable billing integration verified.

26.02.02.context: A callback claims that a payment succeeded.
26.02.02.concept: Verify provider-specific signatures over required bytes and timestamp before trusting any billing event.
26.02.02.exercise: Use a real sandbox provider's documented signing fixture; reject altered bytes and stale timestamps.
26.02.02.positive: Valid signed event is accepted once.
26.02.02.negative: Invalid signature or caller-supplied tenant routing fails.
26.02.02.boundary: Synthetic entitlement policy; no payment provider authenticity, tax, invoicing, real charges or durable billing integration verified.

26.02.03.context: The same invoice payment notification arrives twice.
26.02.03.concept: Durable event IDs and transactional entitlement changes prevent duplicate grants.
26.02.03.exercise: Use synthetic duplicate and conflicting events; compare the P5 transactional inbox contract.
26.02.03.positive: One logical event changes entitlement once.
26.02.03.negative: Duplicate credit or changed payload with same ID fails.
26.02.03.boundary: Synthetic entitlement policy; no payment provider authenticity, tax, invoicing, real charges or durable billing integration verified.

26.02.04.concept: Grace periods and dunning require explicit policy, paid-through date and customer communications.
26.02.04.exercise: Run entitlement for past_due before and at paidUntil; define notification schedule.
26.02.04.negative: Unbounded grace or immediate denial contrary to policy fails.
26.02.04.boundary: Synthetic entitlement policy; no payment provider authenticity, tax, invoicing, real charges or durable billing integration verified.

26.02.05.context: An API bills by consumed units.
26.02.05.concept: Metering records immutable usage identity, unit, time, tenant and aggregation window; reconcile late or duplicate events.
26.02.05.exercise: Create ten synthetic usage records including one duplicate; aggregate unique records and compare invoice line.
26.02.05.positive: Billable units reconcile with source records.
26.02.05.negative: Duplicate events or mixed tenant usage inflate the invoice.
26.02.05.boundary: Synthetic entitlement policy; no payment provider authenticity, tax, invoicing, real charges or durable billing integration verified.

26.02.06.context: A business may switch payment providers.
26.02.06.concept: An adapter maps external statuses and events into internal contracts while retaining provider IDs and audit evidence.
26.02.06.exercise: Define mock provider adapter for normalized subscription status and unsupported event.
26.02.06.positive: Both supported providers can produce same internal state contract.
26.02.06.negative: Unknown event silently activating subscription fails.
26.02.06.boundary: Synthetic entitlement policy; no payment provider authenticity, tax, invoicing, real charges or durable billing integration verified.

26.02.07.context: A billing feature needs a test without real charges.
26.02.07.concept: Use sandbox credentials, synthetic accounts and isolated webhook routing; separate test from live data.
26.02.07.exercise: Rehearse renewal, decline, duplicate delivery and cancellation in an authorized provider sandbox.
26.02.07.positive: Test state changes match expectations with no live charge.
26.02.07.negative: Live credential or missing callback evidence blocks qualification.
26.02.07.boundary: Synthetic entitlement policy; no payment provider authenticity, tax, invoicing, real charges or durable billing integration verified.

26.02.08.context: A learner builds a billing simulator.
26.02.08.concept: Subscription state, webhook verification, idempotency, paid-through access and reconciliation are independent controls.
26.02.08.exercise: Run entitlement tests, design a synthetic event ledger and replay out-of-order renewal and cancellation.
26.02.08.positive: Entitlement follows reviewed state and paid-through date.
26.02.08.negative: A stale event reviving canceled access or duplicate credit fails.
26.02.08.boundary: Synthetic entitlement policy; no payment provider authenticity, tax, invoicing, real charges or durable billing integration verified.

26.03.01.context: An organization cannot explain where personal data is stored.
26.03.01.concept: A data inventory identifies data categories, purpose, systems, recipients, owners, retention and access paths.
26.03.01.exercise: Map synthetic account, billing and log datasets; assign owner and legitimate purpose.
26.03.01.positive: Each dataset has documented processing and access boundaries.
26.03.01.negative: Unknown collection or unowned sensitive dataset fails review.
26.03.01.boundary: Synthetic retention review model only; not legal advice or proof of compliance. Verify current law and organization-specific obligations with qualified counsel.

26.03.02.context: A service operates in the Philippines and serves EU users.
26.03.02.concept: GDPR and the Philippine Data Privacy Act establish distinct privacy frameworks; applicability depends on facts and jurisdiction.
26.03.02.exercise: Compare official texts and regulator guidance for a hypothetical service; document questions for counsel rather than assuming identical obligations.
26.03.02.positive: Analysis distinguishes frameworks, scope and unresolved applicability.
26.03.02.negative: A generic checklist presented as legal compliance fails.
26.03.02.boundary: Synthetic retention review model only; not legal advice or proof of compliance. Verify current law and organization-specific obligations with qualified counsel.

26.03.03.context: A user withdraws optional marketing consent.
26.03.03.concept: Record purpose, lawful basis or consent where applicable, withdrawal and a reviewed retention policy; do not conflate consent with every processing basis.
26.03.03.exercise: Design a synthetic preference history and retention table; test withdrawal without deleting unrelated required records.
26.03.03.positive: Optional processing stops according to policy.
26.03.03.negative: Continued optional processing or blanket deletion without review fails.
26.03.03.boundary: Synthetic retention review model only; not legal advice or proof of compliance. Verify current law and organization-specific obligations with qualified counsel.

26.03.04.context: A person requests access to or deletion of account data.
26.03.04.concept: Verify requester identity, scope, exemptions and legal holds; coordinate across systems and record disposition.
26.03.04.exercise: Create a synthetic export request and deletion workflow with hold and backup handling.
26.03.04.positive: Only authorized export is delivered; deletion eligibility reviewed.
26.03.04.negative: Foreign-account export or ignoring a legal hold fails.
26.03.04.boundary: Synthetic retention review model only; not legal advice or proof of compliance. Verify current law and organization-specific obligations with qualified counsel.

26.03.05.context: An encrypted database backup needs key rotation.
26.03.05.concept: Key lifecycle includes generation, storage, access, versioning, rotation, recovery and destruction; encryption alone is insufficient.
26.03.05.exercise: Design synthetic key versions and restore old ciphertext with approved key, then rotate new writes.
26.03.05.positive: Authorized recovery works under documented versions.
26.03.05.negative: Lost key, exposed key or untested rotation fails.
26.03.05.boundary: Synthetic retention review model only; not legal advice or proof of compliance. Verify current law and organization-specific obligations with qualified counsel.

26.03.06.context: A vendor stores backups in a different region.
26.03.06.concept: Data residency maps where processing and copies occur; cross-border transfer obligations require separate legal assessment.
26.03.06.exercise: Draw data flow for app, backups, telemetry and support; identify unknown locations and contract questions.
26.03.06.positive: Every processing location and owner is known or flagged.
26.03.06.negative: Assuming a database region guarantees all processing stays there fails.
26.03.06.boundary: Synthetic retention review model only; not legal advice or proof of compliance. Verify current law and organization-specific obligations with qualified counsel.

26.03.07.context: A security team needs evidence for an audit.
26.03.07.concept: Controls define expected behavior; evidence must be scoped, dated, traceable and reviewed rather than self-certified.
26.03.07.exercise: Build a synthetic control register with owner, evidence link, test date and exception expiry.
26.03.07.positive: Each control maps to actual evidence or explicitly not-run.
26.03.07.negative: Missing or expired evidence cannot count as compliant.
26.03.07.boundary: Synthetic retention review model only; not legal advice or proof of compliance. Verify current law and organization-specific obligations with qualified counsel.

26.03.08.context: A learner designs a retention job.
26.03.08.concept: Expiry identifies candidates for review; holds, applicable legal duties and safe execution remain separate.
26.03.08.exercise: Run retentionDecision at exact cutoff with and without legal hold; produce dry-run candidate list and approval process.
26.03.08.positive: Eligible items are reviewable; held records retained.
26.03.08.negative: Automatic irreversible deletion on a boolean alone fails.
26.03.08.boundary: Synthetic retention review model only; not legal advice or proof of compliance. Verify current law and organization-specific obligations with qualified counsel.

26.04.01.concept: Audit queries need tenant scope, bounded filters, pagination, redaction and export authorization.
26.04.01.exercise: Design synthetic audit rows for two tenants and a scoped query/export contract.
26.04.01.positive: Only permitted records and fields appear.
26.04.01.negative: Foreign-tenant records or secrets in export fail.
26.04.01.boundary: Synthetic tenant-admin authorization model only; actual RBAC, audit integrity, support workflows and migration safety require runtime acceptance.

26.04.02.context: An operator wants to enable an experimental feature.
26.04.02.concept: Flags require scope, safe default, owner, audit and expiry; not a replacement for permissions.
26.04.02.exercise: Model a tenant-specific flag change with role and reason, test foreign target.
26.04.02.positive: Authorized flag change is scoped and auditable.
26.04.02.negative: A flag granting unauthorized access fails.
26.04.02.boundary: Synthetic tenant-admin authorization model only; actual RBAC, audit integrity, support workflows and migration safety require runtime acceptance.

26.04.03.context: A service changes its runtime configuration.
26.04.03.concept: Configuration needs schema validation, version, secret separation, rollback and clear precedence.
26.04.03.exercise: Design synthetic versioned configuration and reject invalid port or unknown setting.
26.04.03.positive: Valid update preserves previous version for rollback.
26.04.03.negative: Secret in public config or invalid update applied fails.
26.04.03.boundary: Synthetic tenant-admin authorization model only; actual RBAC, audit integrity, support workflows and migration safety require runtime acceptance.

26.04.04.context: A tenant admin invites a member.
26.04.04.concept: Administrative authority is restricted to own tenant and permitted role transitions.
26.04.04.exercise: Run adminAllowed with same and foreign tenant; design real invite and role-assignment tests.
26.04.04.positive: Same-tenant admin can perform intended action.
26.04.04.negative: Foreign tenant or ordinary member is denied.
26.04.04.boundary: Synthetic tenant-admin authorization model only; actual RBAC, audit integrity, support workflows and migration safety require runtime acceptance.

26.04.05.context: Support needs to investigate a customer issue.
26.04.05.concept: Use least-privilege support access, time limits, purpose and audit; avoid silent unrestricted impersonation.
26.04.05.exercise: Design a synthetic support ticket linked to read-only access approval and expiry.
26.04.05.positive: Actions remain scoped to approved ticket and tenant.
26.04.05.negative: Unlogged impersonation or broad write access fails.
26.04.05.boundary: Synthetic tenant-admin authorization model only; actual RBAC, audit integrity, support workflows and migration safety require runtime acceptance.

26.04.06.concept: Abuse management combines bounded rate controls, review, appeals, and scoped enforcement.
26.04.06.exercise: Design synthetic abuse cases with temporary restriction, reviewer decision and false-positive appeal.
26.04.06.positive: Restrictions have reason and expiry or review path.
26.04.06.negative: Silent permanent ban or broad tenant-wide penalty without policy fails.
26.04.06.boundary: Synthetic tenant-admin authorization model only; actual RBAC, audit integrity, support workflows and migration safety require runtime acceptance.

26.04.07.context: A customer imports historical records from CSV.
26.04.07.concept: Imports need staged validation, mapping, dry run, dedupe, transaction and restart plan.
26.04.07.exercise: Create synthetic CSV with valid, duplicate and invalid rows; rehearse dry-run and rejected-row report.
26.04.07.positive: Valid records map consistently; failures are traceable.
26.04.07.negative: Partial silent import or cross-tenant mapping fails.
26.04.07.boundary: Synthetic tenant-admin authorization model only; actual RBAC, audit integrity, support workflows and migration safety require runtime acceptance.

26.04.08.context: A learner designs an administrative console.
26.04.08.concept: Privileged UI must enforce server authorization for every operation, with reason, confirmation and audit for sensitive actions.
26.04.08.exercise: Run adminAllowed; implement a disposable scoped settings action with denial and audit assertions.
26.04.08.positive: Authorized action recorded, unauthorized action blocked.
26.04.08.negative: Client-only permission check or missing audit evidence fails.
26.04.08.boundary: Synthetic tenant-admin authorization model only; actual RBAC, audit integrity, support workflows and migration safety require runtime acceptance.

27.01.01.context: A small team proposes a multi-tenant task workspace.
27.01.01.concept: Requirements distinguish actors, core journeys, constraints, non-goals and measurable acceptance.
27.01.01.exercise: Write scope for sign-in, task editing and organization separation; exclude optional billing and mobile from first release.
27.01.01.positive: Each must-have has a testable outcome.
27.01.01.negative: Unbounded feature list without acceptance fails.
27.01.01.boundary: Capstone rubric checks supplied evidence flags only; no actual app build, SEO, browser or accessibility verification.

27.01.02.context: A team must choose a frontend/backend stack.
27.01.02.concept: An ADR records problem, alternatives, decision, consequences and conditions for reversal.
27.01.02.exercise: Compare a Next-only service with Next plus Nest backend; record constraints and why one is selected.
27.01.02.positive: Choice is tied to scope and tradeoffs.
27.01.02.negative: Framework preference without reasons or migration cost fails.
27.01.02.boundary: Capstone rubric checks supplied evidence flags only; no actual app build, SEO, browser or accessibility verification.

27.01.03.context: A user needs to find tasks and account settings.
27.01.03.concept: Information architecture maps pages, navigation, hierarchy, auth boundaries and empty/error states.
27.01.03.exercise: Create route inventory and task-flow diagram for public and protected pages.
27.01.03.positive: Core tasks can be completed with predictable navigation.
27.01.03.negative: Protected page linked without authorization or dead-end error fails.
27.01.03.boundary: Capstone rubric checks supplied evidence flags only; no actual app build, SEO, browser or accessibility verification.

27.01.04.concept: A component library defines semantic primitives, tokens, variants and accessible interaction states.
27.01.04.exercise: Build local button, input, dialog and table examples with keyboard and dark/light states.
27.01.04.positive: Components retain readable labels and focus.
27.01.04.negative: Visual consistency hiding inaccessible interactions fails.
27.01.04.boundary: Capstone rubric checks supplied evidence flags only; no actual app build, SEO, browser or accessibility verification.

27.01.05.context: A public product site must be discoverable.
27.01.05.concept: SEO requires meaningful content, metadata, canonical URLs, crawl rules and performance; protected content stays private.
27.01.05.exercise: Build a disposable public page and inspect rendered title, canonical, links and robots policy.
27.01.05.positive: Public content discoverable and private content not indexed.
27.01.05.negative: Private workspace included in public sitemap fails.
27.01.05.boundary: Capstone rubric checks supplied evidence flags only; no actual app build, SEO, browser or accessibility verification.

27.01.06.context: A signed-in user opens a workspace.
27.01.06.concept: Server verifies identity and membership; client routes reflect authorization but are not the boundary.
27.01.06.exercise: Implement local session fixture and authorized/anonymous/foreign workspace navigation tests.
27.01.06.negative: Foreign data or protected route relying only on UI guard fails.
27.01.06.boundary: Capstone rubric checks supplied evidence flags only; no actual app build, SEO, browser or accessibility verification.

27.01.07.context: A keyboard-only user completes a task.
27.01.07.concept: Accessibility acceptance requires keyboard, focus, label, contrast, zoom and assistive technology review.
27.01.07.exercise: Complete a local task flow with keyboard and 200% zoom; record screen-reader observations.
27.01.07.positive: User can complete and recover from errors.
27.01.07.negative: Trapped focus, unreadable text or unlabeled control fails.
27.01.07.boundary: Capstone rubric checks supplied evidence flags only; no actual app build, SEO, browser or accessibility verification.

27.01.08.context: A learner reviews the web milestone.
27.01.08.concept: Release acceptance binds scope, workspace behavior, SEO and accessibility evidence to an exact commit.
27.01.08.exercise: Run webAcceptance rubric, attach actual build and browser evidence for each required item.
27.01.08.positive: Every required artifact is reviewed separately.
27.01.08.negative: Passing boolean fixture alone cannot release the app.
27.01.08.boundary: Capstone rubric checks supplied evidence flags only; no actual app build, SEO, browser or accessibility verification.

27.02.01.context: A frontend and API disagree about task payload.
27.02.01.concept: OpenAPI describes the HTTP contract; runtime validation enforces trusted boundaries. Keep schemas and generated clients aligned.
27.02.01.exercise: Define create-task request/response with Zod and OpenAPI; test invalid length and unknown fields.
27.02.01.negative: Invalid body or divergent schema fails.
27.02.01.boundary: Capstone API status/DTO rubric only; no live NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Supabase or JWT validation established.

27.02.02.context: A backend mixes auth, task rules and database access.
27.02.02.concept: Nest modules separate ownership, controllers, use cases and injected infrastructure.
27.02.02.exercise: Create disposable task module with repository port and auth guard; test dependency injection.
27.02.02.positive: Use case has explicit dependencies and route contract.
27.02.02.boundary: Capstone API status/DTO rubric only; no live NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Supabase or JWT validation established.

27.02.03.context: A task table must support many organizations.
27.02.03.concept: Relational constraints and migrations enforce stable IDs, tenant relationships and invariants.
27.02.03.exercise: Create disposable PostgreSQL migration for organizations, members and tasks; test foreign-key violation and rollback.
27.02.03.positive: Valid rows persist; invalid relationships denied.
27.02.03.negative: Cross-tenant relationship or unreviewed destructive migration fails.
27.02.03.boundary: Capstone API status/DTO rubric only; no live NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Supabase or JWT validation established.

27.02.04.context: A service uses Prisma for persistence.
27.02.04.concept: Repository adapters map validated domain requests to scoped database queries; generated types are not authorization.
27.02.04.exercise: Implement disposable Prisma task repository and test tenant filter, pagination and transaction behavior.
27.02.04.positive: Own tenant queries return expected rows.
27.02.04.negative: Unscoped find/update or query leakage fails.
27.02.04.boundary: Capstone API status/DTO rubric only; no live NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Supabase or JWT validation established.

27.02.05.context: An API receives a Supabase access token.
27.02.05.concept: Validate trusted issuer, signature, audience, time and key rotation using supported verification; never trust merely decoded claims.
27.02.05.exercise: Use authorized local/sandbox Supabase and documented JWT validation; test expired, tampered and wrong audience tokens.
27.02.05.positive: Only verified valid token establishes identity.
27.02.05.negative: Unsigned or decoded-only token accepted fails.
27.02.05.boundary: Capstone API status/DTO rubric only; no live NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Supabase or JWT validation established.

27.02.06.context: A user guesses another organization's task ID.
27.02.06.concept: Tenant membership and permissions must be checked server-side and backed by appropriate database policies.
27.02.06.exercise: Run apiAcceptance synthetic statuses; execute actual own/anonymous/foreign requests in disposable DB/API.
27.02.06.positive: Owner 200, anonymous 401, foreign 404 by chosen contract.
27.02.06.negative: Foreign record or private field exposed fails.
27.02.06.boundary: Capstone API status/DTO rubric only; no live NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Supabase or JWT validation established.

27.02.07.context: A backend release changes routing and persistence.
27.02.07.concept: Integration tests cross actual server, database and auth boundaries with isolated fixtures.
27.02.07.exercise: Boot API on loopback with disposable DB; run create/read/update/deny and rollback tests.
27.02.07.positive: Expected data and response changes match.
27.02.07.negative: Mock-only tests cannot establish actual DB behavior.
27.02.07.boundary: Capstone API status/DTO rubric only; no live NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Supabase or JWT validation established.

27.02.08.context: A learner defends secured API milestone.
27.02.08.concept: Review contracts, migrations, auth verification, isolation, tests and recorded exact commit before accepting.
27.02.08.exercise: Run apiAcceptance; gather actual request traces and DB role tests for all required cases.
27.02.08.positive: Evidence establishes documented authorization and DTO policy.
27.02.08.negative: Missing negative test, secret exposure or wrong commit blocks review.
27.02.08.boundary: Capstone API status/DTO rubric only; no live NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Supabase or JWT validation established.

27.03.01.context: A workspace lists thousands of tasks.
27.03.01.concept: CRUD contracts include bounded pagination, stable ordering, validation and scoped writes.
27.03.01.exercise: Build local paginated list with same-sort values and invalid cursor; test owner and foreign tenant.
27.03.01.positive: Pages contain each intended row without duplicates.
27.03.01.negative: Unbounded result or cross-tenant cursor accepted fails.
27.03.01.boundary: Synthetic integrated-feature rubric; actual upload, mail, Redis, websocket, search and audit behavior require live isolated tests.

27.03.02.context: A user attaches a file to a task.
27.03.02.concept: Validate bytes, size, type, ownership and scan/quarantine before authorized access.
27.03.02.exercise: Use disposable upload fixture with valid file and mismatched content; verify denied access while pending.
27.03.02.positive: Clean authorized file becomes accessible after review.
27.03.02.negative: Mismatched or quarantined object exposed fails.
27.03.02.boundary: Synthetic integrated-feature rubric; actual upload, mail, Redis, websocket, search and audit behavior require live isolated tests.

27.03.03.context: A task assignment sends a notification.
27.03.03.concept: Durable queue and outbox separate transaction from external delivery; retries need stable identifiers.
27.03.03.exercise: Implement a disposable assignment/outbox transaction and fake sender with duplicate and failed delivery.
27.03.03.positive: One logical notification is tracked with retry outcome.
27.03.03.negative: Email sent for rolled-back assignment or duplicate effect fails.
27.03.03.boundary: Synthetic integrated-feature rubric; actual upload, mail, Redis, websocket, search and audit behavior require live isolated tests.

27.03.04.context: A task update makes cached list data stale.
27.03.04.concept: Invalidate or version derived caches after committed writes; keys must include appropriate tenant scope.
27.03.04.exercise: Use disposable Redis and synthetic tasks; warm cache, update, invalidate and test another tenant.
27.03.04.positive: Updated own list converges; foreign cache isolated.
27.03.04.negative: Stale data permanently retained or cross-tenant leakage fails.
27.03.04.boundary: Synthetic integrated-feature rubric; actual upload, mail, Redis, websocket, search and audit behavior require live isolated tests.

27.03.05.context: A teammate receives task changes in real time.
27.03.05.concept: Live updates need authorization, scoped subscriptions, versioning and reconnect reconciliation.
27.03.05.exercise: Use local websocket/SSE fixture with two tenants; drop connection and replay missed updates.
27.03.05.positive: Authorized updates arrive and reconnect converges.
27.03.05.negative: Foreign event or stale state after reconnect fails.
27.03.05.boundary: Synthetic integrated-feature rubric; actual upload, mail, Redis, websocket, search and audit behavior require live isolated tests.

27.03.06.context: A user searches many task descriptions.
27.03.06.concept: Search applies tenant/ACL filters before ranking and returns bounded results; index updates need freshness contract.
27.03.06.exercise: Seed disposable search with similar terms in two tenants; test query, pagination and stale update.
27.03.06.negative: Foreign result or unbounded search fails.
27.03.06.boundary: Synthetic integrated-feature rubric; actual upload, mail, Redis, websocket, search and audit behavior require live isolated tests.

27.03.07.context: An admin needs to explain a task change.
27.03.07.concept: Audit trail records actor, action, target, outcome and time; sensitive content excluded.
27.03.07.exercise: Create, edit and deny synthetic actions; inspect scoped audit output and replay correlation.
27.03.07.positive: Relevant events are traceable without secrets.
27.03.07.negative: Missing denied action or editable unaudited history fails.
27.03.07.boundary: Synthetic integrated-feature rubric; actual upload, mail, Redis, websocket, search and audit behavior require live isolated tests.

27.03.08.concept: Cross-feature acceptance verifies behavior, security boundaries, error recovery and audit together.
27.03.08.exercise: Run workspaceAcceptance; execute actual create/upload/notification/cache/live/search flow with negative cases.
27.03.08.positive: Required journey works with isolation and audit evidence.
27.03.08.negative: Passing isolated units but failing integrated journey blocks milestone.
27.03.08.boundary: Synthetic integrated-feature rubric; actual upload, mail, Redis, websocket, search and audit behavior require live isolated tests.

27.04.01.context: A local app needs a reproducible multi-service environment.
27.04.01.concept: Compose declares service dependencies, private networking, volumes, env boundaries and health checks.
27.04.01.exercise: Create a disposable stack with app and DB; use synthetic secrets and inspect port exposure and readiness.
27.04.01.positive: Stack starts reproducibly and DB is private.
27.04.01.negative: Public DB or credentials in committed env fails.
27.04.01.boundary: Capstone readiness rubric only; no container, deployment, scan, benchmark or restore is verified by supplied booleans.

27.04.02.context: A candidate commit must pass repeatable checks.
27.04.02.concept: CI specifies immutable inputs, required jobs and exact-commit evidence; local qualification can precede hosted automation.
27.04.02.exercise: Use existing local coordinator and design required lint/type/test/build jobs without enabling Actions.
27.04.02.positive: Required checks have actual matching results.
27.04.02.negative: Skipped or stale job cannot pass.
27.04.02.boundary: Capstone readiness rubric only; no container, deployment, scan, benchmark or restore is verified by supplied booleans.

27.04.03.context: A new release must be reversible.
27.04.03.concept: Deploy a reviewed immutable artifact, verify compatibility and health, define rollback and migration recovery.
27.04.03.exercise: Rehearse a disposable release with failed smoke and rollback to prior known version.
27.04.03.positive: Rollback restores intended service and preserves data.
27.04.03.negative: Incompatible destructive change or unverified rollback fails.
27.04.03.boundary: Capstone readiness rubric only; no container, deployment, scan, benchmark or restore is verified by supplied booleans.

27.04.04.context: An API failure must be detectable.
27.04.04.concept: Logs, metrics, traces and alerts should describe user impact without leaking data; ownership and runbooks matter.
27.04.04.exercise: Instrument isolated API, trigger bounded failure and verify alert/runbook path.
27.04.04.negative: Secret logging or unowned noisy alerts fail.
27.04.04.boundary: Capstone readiness rubric only; no container, deployment, scan, benchmark or restore is verified by supplied booleans.

27.04.05.context: A release may introduce authorization and dependency regressions.
27.04.05.concept: Security verification needs concrete abuse cases, dependency review and relevant trust boundaries.
27.04.05.exercise: Run scoped auth tests, secret scan and current dependency audit on exact candidate; triage findings.
27.04.05.positive: Blocking findings resolved or explicitly held.
27.04.05.negative: Scanner outage or foreign tenant access fails.
27.04.05.boundary: Capstone readiness rubric only; no container, deployment, scan, benchmark or restore is verified by supplied booleans.

27.04.06.context: A service must meet a defined latency target.
27.04.06.concept: Performance qualification uses matched workloads, thresholds, errors and repeatable conditions.
27.04.06.exercise: Benchmark disposable API with bounded k6 or equivalent; record p95, errors and resource usage.
27.04.06.negative: Dropping failures or claiming synthetic samples as real benchmark fails.
27.04.06.boundary: Capstone readiness rubric only; no container, deployment, scan, benchmark or restore is verified by supplied booleans.

27.04.07.context: A backup exists but recovery has never been tested.
27.04.07.concept: Restore drills verify data, application behavior, recovery time and loss objectives.
27.04.07.exercise: Restore synthetic backup into separate disposable DB; compare counts and use-case results.
27.04.07.positive: Restored data and elapsed recovery are recorded.
27.04.07.negative: Backup-only evidence or failed validation blocks readiness.
27.04.07.boundary: Capstone readiness rubric only; no container, deployment, scan, benchmark or restore is verified by supplied booleans.

27.04.08.concept: Acceptance includes build, security, observability, rollback and tested restore, plus manual review of remaining risks.
27.04.08.exercise: Run productionAcceptance; attach actual candidate-specific evidence and signoff for each item.
27.04.08.positive: All required real checks pass or remain explicitly blocked.
27.04.08.negative: Missing restore, failed security or false evidence cannot authorize launch.
27.04.08.boundary: Capstone readiness rubric only; no container, deployment, scan, benchmark or restore is verified by supplied booleans.

27.05.01.context: A reviewer searches for weaknesses in a learner project.
27.05.01.concept: Authorized security review has defined scope, synthetic accounts, impact limits and responsible reporting.
27.05.01.exercise: Review disposable app for auth, input, secrets and recovery defects; record reproducible findings and fixes.
27.05.01.positive: Findings have impact, reproduction and regression tests.
27.05.01.negative: Testing unapproved external systems or unverifiable claims fails.
27.05.01.boundary: Final defense rubric only; actual human review, exploit verification, performance, costs and upgrade rehearsal remain separate.

27.05.02.context: A dependency fails during a technical defense.
27.05.02.concept: Bounded fault drills demonstrate behavior, fallback, recovery and observability in an isolated environment.
27.05.02.exercise: Inject one synthetic dependency timeout and record impact, abort criteria and restoration.
27.05.02.positive: System follows documented failure behavior and recovers.
27.05.02.negative: Unbounded retries, missing recovery or live-service disruption fails.
27.05.02.boundary: Final defense rubric only; actual human review, exploit verification, performance, costs and upgrade rehearsal remain separate.

27.05.03.context: A learner explains why the system is modular rather than distributed.
27.05.03.concept: Architecture defense compares alternatives using constraints, measurements, failure domains and migration costs.
27.05.03.exercise: Present ADR and diagram; explain when service extraction would become justified.
27.05.03.positive: Decision includes tradeoffs and measurable trigger.
27.05.03.negative: Tool names alone or unsupported scale claims fail.
27.05.03.boundary: Final defense rubric only; actual human review, exploit verification, performance, costs and upgrade rehearsal remain separate.

27.05.04.context: A future maintainer needs to understand the app.
27.05.04.concept: Source and API documentation should cover setup, contracts, architecture, operational limits and troubleshooting.
27.05.04.exercise: Write a fresh-checkout guide and OpenAPI examples; ask another reviewer to follow them.
27.05.04.positive: A reviewer can reproduce supported flow.
27.05.04.negative: Missing prerequisites or invented test outcomes fail.
27.05.04.boundary: Final defense rubric only; actual human review, exploit verification, performance, costs and upgrade rehearsal remain separate.

27.05.05.context: A SaaS prototype needs an operating-cost forecast.
27.05.05.concept: Model workload, storage, transfer, compute, third-party usage and uncertainty; obtain current prices before real commitment.
27.05.05.exercise: Build low/base/high hypothetical monthly demand and costs; document free-tier limits separately.
27.05.05.negative: Ignoring variable usage or presenting hypothetical costs as quotes fails.
27.05.05.boundary: Final defense rubric only; actual human review, exploit verification, performance, costs and upgrade rehearsal remain separate.

27.05.06.context: A graduate wants to publish a portfolio case study.
27.05.06.concept: A credible case study explains problem, design, implementation, verified outcomes and remaining limits.
27.05.06.exercise: Draft one-page project case study with architecture, screenshots from actual app and test evidence.
27.05.06.positive: Claims map to real artifacts and tradeoffs.
27.05.06.negative: Invented production metrics or credentials in screenshots fail.
27.05.06.boundary: Final defense rubric only; actual human review, exploit verification, performance, costs and upgrade rehearsal remain separate.

27.05.07.context: A dependency upgrade may break the system.
27.05.07.concept: Upgrade plan inventories versions, advisories, compatibility, migrations and rollback; test incrementally.
27.05.07.exercise: Create a reviewable upgrade branch for one dependency with lockfile and regression checks.
27.05.07.positive: Actual upgrade diff and test results are recorded.
27.05.07.negative: Fabricated lock or unexplained breaking change fails.
27.05.07.boundary: Final defense rubric only; actual human review, exploit verification, performance, costs and upgrade rehearsal remain separate.

27.05.08.context: A learner completes the technical assessment.
27.05.08.concept: A final defense evaluates implementation evidence, tradeoffs, recovery, cost and documentation, not memorized tool lists.
27.05.08.exercise: Run defenseAcceptance; assemble commit-bound portfolio, demo, negative tests, runbook and independent review rubric.
27.05.08.positive: Reviewer can reproduce core flow and challenge assumptions.
27.05.08.negative: Pending or unverified evidence remains incomplete.
27.05.08.boundary: Final defense rubric only; actual human review, exploit verification, performance, costs and upgrade rehearsal remain separate.
